_comment: Every app-visible change serial 4 makes against serial 3 (scripts/validate.py --declared ci/serial4-declared.json --baseline ci/serial3-baseline.json --previous-ref <serial 3>). Serial 3's own list stays in ci/serial3-declared.json (meshTerm's tests read a byte-identical copy of that one).

changes.reason: The AppArmor branch loads its profile with apparmor_parser -r (no systemd needed; serial 3 restarted apparmor.service, which fails without systemd) and runs only where apparmor_parser exists (no AppArmor userspace: nothing to load into, and a container on a restricting host has no /etc/apparmor.d: the serial-3 GitHub runner failure)
Kali keeps the Debian family's apt text: the same apparmor_parser change
Arch: pacman -Syu --needed (a fresh Arch has no sync database, so -S alone fails 'target not found'; -Syu, never -Sy alone, as sudo.install does, so no partial upgrade)

The unknown-family chain gains zypper and pacman (Containers sends Arch and openSUSE as unknown) and fails with a message where no package manager it knows is found (serial 3 exited 0 having installed nothing)
The unknown-family chain gains zypper (ca-certificates with ca-certificates-mozilla, the bundle) and pacman, and fails with a message where no package manager it knows is found
Arch: get.docker.com refuses it ('Unsupported distribution'); Arch's docker package, enabled and started where systemd runs
Manjaro and EndeavourOS (Arch-based): the Arch text
openSUSE: get.docker.com refuses it; openSUSE's docker package, enabled and started where systemd runs
